title: Visual Target - Crossy Road Style Exploration
summary: Crossy Road voxel art direction applied to Corner. Three office variants + four agent characters. Potential new art direction or style pack.
content:
Visual Target: Crossy Road Style Exploration

Steffen | 2026-03-16 For Patrik. New direction exploration. Crossy Road meets Corner.

The Direction

Crossy Road's visual DNA: chunky voxel geometry, bright saturated colors, characters with maximum personality in minimum geometry, everything feels like it could bounce. Applied to Corner, this creates an office world that feels alive, toylike, collectible, and FUN.

This is a massive tonal shift from the current warm-night north star. The current direction is "premium indie game at night" -- moody, atmospheric, architectural. Crossy Road style is "toy office you want to pick up and play with" -- bright, bouncy, immediate.

Both are valid. They could coexist as style packs in the product.

The Three Office Variants

1. corner-warm-night.png -- Night Mode

The Crossy Road voxel aesthetic applied to the existing warm-night concept. Dark navy background, warm amber light spilling from windows, CORNER sign glowing. Each room has its signature color: Bobby's purple LEDs, Elon's green server glow, Steffen's golden warmth.

What works: Keeps the cozy, alive feeling of the original north star but adds the chunky voxel charm. The CORNER sign pops. Room colors are distinct and readable.

Best for: Default game state. Feels like late-night work mode but playful instead of serious.

2. corner-daylight.png -- Daylight Mode

Bright blue sky, chunky voxel clouds, green grass ground plane with tiny cubic trees. The full Crossy Road environment treatment. Each room is a different bright color. The building sits in a small park-like setting.

What works: This is the most "Crossy Road" of the three. The blue sky, blocky clouds, and green grass are immediately recognizable. The office feels like a place you'd find while hopping through a Crossy Road world. Maximum approachability.

Best for: Onboarding, marketing materials, first impression. This is the "come play" version.

3. corner-celebration.png -- Celebration Mode

Fireworks, confetti, balloons, string lights, party energy. The voxel characters are celebrating. Every room is lit up. The CORNER sign is extra bright with party lights.

Best for: Achievement triggers. When a client signs, when a milestone hits, when an agent completes a major task. The product should CELEBRATE with you. This visual proves the style supports those moments.

The Characters

Four agent characters rendered as Crossy Road unlockable figures. Each one reads instantly as their role through props, colors, and minimal detail choices.

character-bobby.png -- Bobby (Web Dev)

  • Dark hoodie, purple LED headphones
  • Holds a tiny voxel laptop
  • Purple underglow on his grass platform (his signature)
  • Focused but cool expression
  • Signature color: purple (#9C27B0)

character-elon.png -- Elon (Infrastructure)

  • Dark tech outfit, green glowing eyes
  • Wrench in hand, server rack beside him
  • Floating green data cube particles
  • Dark gray platform with green LED dots
  • Signature color: green (#4CAF50)

character-cleo.png -- Cleo (Content)

  • Orange/coral scarf/bandana, dark shirt
  • Holds voxel film camera
  • Clapperboard at feet
  • Warm orange platform with glow
  • Signature color: orange/coral (#FF7043)

character-steffen.png -- Steffen (Design)

  • Black turtleneck, round glasses
  • Paint palette with colorful dots
  • Tiny easel beside him
  • Golden wood platform with paint splatters
  • Signature color: golden (#FFB74D)

Style Comparison: Current vs. Crossy Road

Attribute Current North Star Crossy Road Style
Mood Moody, atmospheric, cozy Bright, bouncy, playful
Geometry Semi-realistic isometric, detailed Ultra-chunky voxels, minimal
Colors Warm amber on dark navy Saturated candy colors
Characters Small detailed figures at desks Chunky collectible figures
Lighting Realistic light pools, shadows Flat shading, minimal shadow
Ground plane Subtle dark surface Green grass, trees, clouds
Wall style Architectural, visible depth Blocky, toy-like
Feel "Premium indie game" "Toy you want to play with"
Emotion Comfort, focus, craft Joy, energy, fun

How This Could Work as Product

Option A: Full Art Direction Pivot

Replace the warm-night style entirely. The product IS Crossy Road style. Everything bounces. Every agent is a collectible character. The daylight version is default, night is an unlockable theme.

Pros: Immediately distinctive. More approachable than moody pixels. The celebration mode creates real emotional moments. Characters become a feature (collect/customize agents).

Cons: Less "premium" feeling. Might not read as "serious business tool" to some clients.

Option B: Style Pack in a Catalog

Keep the warm-night architectural style as default. Crossy Road style is an unlockable or selectable theme. The three-mode product idea (Game, Checklist, Megaboard) already supports this -- each mode could have its own visual style.

Pros: Best of both worlds. The product demonstrates range. "Your Corner, your style."

Cons: More build work. Need to maintain multiple visual systems.

Option C: Crossy Road for Marketing, Architectural for Product

Use the bright daylight Crossy Road style in all marketing materials, landing pages, social media. The actual product interior uses the warm-night architectural style. The shift from marketing to product feels like "entering the real office."

Pros: Marketing gets the maximum approachability. Product feels premium once you're in.

Character Expansion Notes

The four characters generated here (Bobby, Elon, Cleo, Steffen) prove the system works. Every agent in Corner could get one:

  • Mom -- Clipboard, headset, multiple floating status icons around her
  • Alex -- Business suit, globe, strategy book
  • Steve -- Laptop showing database schema, glasses, calculator
  • Jacob -- Phone to ear, stack of business cards, Phoenix map pin
  • Tony -- Ring light, multiple phone screens floating around
  • Colton -- Dual monitors, component blocks, organized desk
  • Elmo -- Magnifying glass, red pen, lab coat, checklist clipboard
  • Patrik -- The boss. Corner office energy. Clean, minimal, premium. Maybe a coffee mug and a camera.

Each character becomes collectible within the product. As clients add agents to their Corner, they unlock new characters. This is the Crossy Road hook: the joy of collecting.

Implementation Notes

If this direction moves forward, the build approach differs from the architectural style:

  1. Voxel assets can be simpler. Fewer polygons, less lighting math. Crossy Road's genius is doing MORE with LESS geometry.
  2. Animation is key. The bouncy hop, the idle wobble, the celebration jump. Without animation, voxel characters are just blocks. WITH animation, they have soul.
  3. Color is the depth cue. Where the architectural style uses lighting for depth, Crossy Road uses color saturation and hue shifts. Front-facing surfaces are brighter. Shadow sides are one shade darker. That's it.
  4. Sound design matters more. Crossy Road's boops, hops, and coin sounds are half the charm. If Corner goes this direction, every action needs a satisfying sound.

This exploration shows what Corner looks like through the Crossy Road lens. Whether it becomes the art direction, a style pack, or marketing-only, the voxel character system is worth developing further. Every agent as a collectible figure is a product feature, not just art.

FULL CONNECTED OFFICE (2026-03-16)

The characters were CLEAN but the original corner backgrounds (corner-warm-night.png, corner-daylight.png, corner-celebration.png) were too detailed. They used semi-realistic pixel art while the characters are chunky voxel. They clashed.

New assets generated to fix this. The WORLD now matches the CHARACTERS.

office-full.png -- Full Office, Daylight

The hero image. Full L-shaped building, all 13 rooms + main hall. Bright blue sky, chunky voxel clouds, green grass ground plane. Every room's signature color visible from overhead. CORNER sign on the facade. This is the Crossy Road world the characters belong in.

office-full-medium.png -- Medium Zoom

Closer view showing 6-8 rooms in detail. Furniture pieces visible as chunky voxel objects. Characters visible at desks. Bobby's purple, Steffen's golden studio, Cleo's coral studio all readable. Proves the style holds at medium zoom.

office-full-close.png -- Close Zoom

4 rooms: Bobby's Dev Lab (purple), Colton's Builder Bay (indigo), Steffen's Design Studio (golden), Main Hall. Characters are prominent Crossy Road figures. Props visible: triple monitors, easel, color wheel, couch. The closest zoom before you'd need individual room renders.

office-full-night.png -- Full Office, Night

Same building as daylight but at night. Dark navy background (#0A0F1E). Each room glows with its signature color against the darkness. Bobby purple, Elon green, Steffen golden. The CORNER sign glows warm amber. Proves the modular system: same geometry, different lighting = different skin.

THE MODULAR SYSTEM (Proven)

Two skins now exist in the catalog:

Skin File Aesthetic Best For
Classic full-office-warm-night.png Detailed pixel art, moody, atmospheric Premium feel, default product interior
Voxel (Day) office-full.png Crossy Road chunky, bright, toylike Marketing, onboarding, approachability
Voxel (Night) office-full-night.png Crossy Road chunky, glowing rooms on dark Default game state, late-night mode

Bobby swaps ONE image URL and the entire world changes style. The characters (character-bobby.png etc.) work in the Voxel world. The detailed pixel art characters from the Classic style are separate assets.

Same engine. Different vibes. Style pack proven.

BOBBY HANDOFF

File path for the Voxel world background: projects/steffen/visual-target/crossy-road-style/office-full.png

What Bobby does:

  1. Use office-full.png (daylight) or office-full-night.png (night) as the base world image
  2. The existing Crossy Road characters (character-bobby.png, character-elon.png, etc.) overlay on top
  3. One image URL swap tests the full modularity of the style system
  4. If the engine supports it: style selector dropdown (Classic / Voxel Day / Voxel Night)

The characters already exist. The world now matches. This is a one-line swap to test.
